newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Treasury's Macciotta confirms surplus hopes.
newsitem.headline: Italy Treasury's Macciotta confirms surplus hopes.

text.p: Italian Treasury undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta on Tuesday confirmed that the government hoped for a record budget surplus of some 30 trillion lire in June.
"It is possible, to some extent we are expecting it," he told reporters, adding that proceeds from individual tax returns were "looking good".
Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore said on Tuesday that these returns were around five trillion lire higher than expected.
Italy had a budget surplus of 25 trillion lire in June 1996.

"Things are going well and we haven't ruled out (a 30 trillion lire surplus)," Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco told reporters. "We were very perplexed. With the climate for production very tough, this may signal a turnaround."
A budget surplus in the order of 30 trillion lire would slash Italy's first half public sector borrowing requirement to around 25 trillion lire from 54 trillion in the same 1996 period.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has repeatedly forecast a lower first-half PSBR compared with last year, in line with the government's target of cutting the ratio of deficit to gross domestic product to the three percent goal to join the European Union's planned single currency in 1999.
Employers' body Confindustria has said that Italy will need a surplus of around 30 trillion lire in June to keep accounts on course for the three percent deficit/GDP target.
